summary: The adult of the Goldeen line, a horned river fish whose life centres on its nest. In autumn Seaking gather from all over to spawn, turning the rivers red; the male bores a hole in a riverbed boulder with his drill-like horn, and the pair take turns guarding the eggs for over a month. It defends its eggs with its life. In the highlands it is a rare Super Rod catch in Dark Cave's water, where there are no riverbed boulders to nest in.

anatomy.text: A fish, 1.3 m and 39.0 kg, typed Water.
The horn on its head is sharp like a drill.
In autumn its body becomes fattier and its colours are at their most beautiful, before it courts a mate.

diet.text: No entry says what Seaking eats.
It fattens before the autumn courtship, so it must feed heavily in the months before spawning.
Its level-up moves start with Poison Jab and Peck (Lv 1); like Goldeen's, they are strikes that might double as feeding, but nothing says so.

habitat.text: Rivers, creeks and stream beds; it lives in hollowed rocks in streams.

In the highlands in HeartGold and SoulSilver it is only in Dark Cave's water, both ends, by Super Rod 10% (Lv 40). It is widespread elsewhere: Union Cave, Slowpoke Well, Route 42, Mt. Mortar (also surfing 10%), Tohjo Falls, the Kanto routes and the Johto Safari Zone, and it is the main surfing encounter on Mt. Silver (about 90%). The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is waters-edge.
A boulder-nesting river fish recorded in a cave pool: Dark Cave Seaking presumably feed there and spawn somewhere with current and boulders.
habitat.note: Nothing records where Dark Cave's fish breed.

behavior.text: In the autumn spawning season they swim powerfully up rivers and creeks.
Males perform courtship dances in riverbeds to woo females.
Males patrol the area around their nests in autumn to protect their offspring.

social.text: During spawning season Seaking gather from all over, colouring the rivers a brilliant red.
social.analogy: Sockeye salmon (Oncorhynchus nerka) turn bright red at spawning, and their mass runs colour whole rivers.

social.text: The male and female take turns patrolling around their nest and eggs.

reproduction.text: The male makes the nest by carving out a boulder in the stream with his horn.
reproduction.analogy: Male three-spined sticklebacks (Gasterosteus aculeatus) build the nest, take on red breeding colours and guard the eggs and young.

reproduction.text: The hole stops the eggs from washing away in the current or being attacked.
It is very protective: the guarding of eggs goes on for over a month, and it defends them with its life.
Water 2 egg group, 20 egg cycles, even sex ratio; the line's egg moves sit on Goldeen.

defense.text: To protect its family it will fight with its drill-sharp horn.
Swift Swim and Water Veil, as Goldeen; Agility (Lv 56) and Aqua Ring (Lv 27).

senses.text: Nothing is said about its senses.

life_cycle.text: It evolves from Goldeen at Lv 33.
Both stages are described spawning, Goldeen in schools running upstream and Seaking at nests, so the line may breed before it reaches full size.

moves_in_the_wild.text: Horn Drill (Lv 47) is the nest-borer in game form; Horn Attack, Fury Attack and Megahorn (Lv 63) are the horn as a weapon. Waterfall (Lv 40) is a natural move, matching the runs upstream.

ecology.text: An engineer: it bores holes in riverbed boulders, and empty nest holes would shelter other small stream animals.
ecology.note: The boring is canon; later use of the holes by others is not recorded.

ecology.text: A mass autumn gathering of large fish is a seasonal food pulse for predators; none is recorded in the highlands.
Its diet, and so its trophic level, is unknown.

humans.text: Its autumn spawning is a spectacle: rivers turn a brilliant red.
Anyone working a stream in autumn should leave nest boulders alone: the guarding parent will fight.

homestead.text: To breed it needs a real stream with boulders; a pond will not do.
Expect it to be aggressive near its nest for over a month each autumn; keep people and stock out of that stretch of stream.
Its horn bores holes in stone; whether it would do so anywhere but at a nest is unknown.
A pair of Seaking in the homestead's stream, with the autumn red run as the household's marker of the year turning.

niche.foraging: unknown; nothing records what it eats

relationships.note: Nest sites, bored with the horn.
Empty nest holes as shelter; not recorded.

ecotypes.name: Torrent spawner
ecotypes.reading: Two powerful water attacks in a lineage built for the autumn run up steep, fast streams. Fits highland streams with falls, where the strongest swimmers reach the best nest boulders.

ecotypes.name: Silt nester
ecotypes.reading: Mud moves in a lineage that nests where boulders are scarce, digging into silt and gravel instead of boring rock. Fits slow, muddy reaches and cave pools such as Dark Cave's.
ecotypes.behavior: Digs a hollow rather than drilling one.

ecotypes.name: Heavy guardian
ecotypes.reading: Weight and a tail strike in a nest-guarding lineage that drives intruders off by force. Fits crowded spawning reaches where many pairs nest close together, as when Seaking gather from all over.
ecotypes.behavior: Guards longer and fights harder at the nest.

open_questions: What does Seaking eat, especially to fatten in autumn (119.13)?
Where do Dark Cave's Seaking spawn? A cave pool has no riverbed boulders.
Which season: spring for Goldeen (118.8), autumn for Seaking?
Who guards: the males (119.5) or both parents in turn (119.7)?
What uses the bored nest holes after the young leave?
What eats Seaking or its eggs? Nothing is recorded.

contradictions.text: Crystal says the males patrol the nests in autumn; Sapphire says the male and female take turns patrolling.
contradictions.reading: Male-only versus shared guarding. Possibly both happen; not resolved here.

contradictions.text: Emerald puts Goldeen's spawning runs in spring; the Seaking entries put spawning in autumn.
contradictions.reading: The two stages may spawn in different seasons, or the entries disagree.
